rulings.restated: Enter the amount from helper "The maximum section 179 deduction limitation for 2025".
rulings.model: The line 1 instructions say 'Generally, the maximum section 179 expense deduction is $2,500,000.' But Worksheet 1 says to enter on Form 4562, line 1 'the smaller of line 1 or line 2' (total cost or $2,500,000). Using the full $2,500,000 when cost is lower can change line 5, line 11 and the carryover on line 13 when there is a 2024 carryover. The text does not say which governs.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: ambiguity; i4562 p. 4, Line 1: "Generally, the maximum section 179 expense deduction is $2,500,000 for section 179 property (including qualified section 179 real property) placed in service during the tax year beginning in 2025."; "Tip: You can use Worksheet 1 to assist you in determining the amount to enter on line 1."; Worksheet 1: "3. Enter the smaller of line 1 or line 2 here ... 4. Enter the amount from line 3 here and on Form 4562, line 1". The model reads Worksheet 1 as fixing line 1 at the smaller of the cost and $2,500,000; the project follows the line 1 instruction on the same page, which states the maximum as $2,500,000 and offers the worksheet as an aid. amb.2025.s179_carryover_no_property records the model's reading as the alternative and the owner adopted the project's (TASKS T-043; ambiguities/research/amb.2025.s179_carryover_no_property.md). The English says what the project computes and names the register entry ("Interpretation: amb.2025.s179_carryover_no_property"); lines 5, 11 and 13 change with line 1 as the model says, by design.

rulings.restated: Enter the amount from helper "The maximum section 179 deduction limitation for 2025".
rulings.model: The restatement always enters $2,500,000. Worksheet 1 says 'Enter the smaller of line 1 [total cost of section 179 property] or line 2 [$2,500,000] here' and 'Enter the amount from line 3 here and on Form 4562, line 1'. When total cost is under $2,500,000, line 1 should be that cost, which also changes lines 5 and 11.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: project retained (owner, T-043; amb.2025.s179_carryover_no_property). The model reads Worksheet 1 (i4562 p. 4) as fixing line 1 at the smaller of the cost and $2,500,000. The line 1 instruction on the same page states the maximum as $2,500,000 and offers the worksheet as an optional aid. With line 1 at $2,500,000, lines 5, 9, 11 and 12 compute 26 U.S.C. 179(b)(3)(B) exactly; the worksheet's cap changes no return without a carryover and wrongly withholds a carryover on one (ambiguities/research/amb.2025.s179_carryover_no_property.md). Lines 5 and 11 change as the model says, by design.

rulings.restated: Enter the smaller of helper "That income, if zero or less zero" or line 5.
rulings.model: The IRS text uses 'the total taxable income from any trade or business you actively conducted, computed without regard to any section 179 expense deduction, the deduction for one-half of self-employment taxes ... or any net operating loss deduction,' plus wages. The restatement counts only Schedule C net profit plus Form 1040 line 1a. It has no refusal for other actively conducted businesses (for example partnership or S corporation business income, which line 6 contemplates for K-1 section 179 amounts) or for Schedule C activities that are not actively conducted, so those cases would change the value.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: refusal located elsewhere; restatement accepted. The only trades or businesses on a return in scope are the Schedule C businesses (partnerships, S corporations, Schedule E and farm income are refused through scope.schedule1 and qbi.unsupported), each materially participated in (sc.passive; a passive activity is refused), which is active conduct; wages are Form 1040 line 1a (i4562 p. 5, Line 11, 'include all wages, salaries, tips, and other compensation you earned as an employee'). So the income the instruction names is the Schedule C net profit before the section 179 deduction plus line 1a.

rulings.restated: Subtract line 12 from helper "Add lines 9 and 10". If zero or less, enter -0-.
rulings.model: The form says 'Add lines 9 and 10, less line 12.' However, when line 5 is zero the instructions say to 'enter the carryover of any disallowed deduction from 2024 ... on line 13'. The program leaves line 10 out in that case, and it is not stated whether the left-out line counts as the carryover or as zero in 'Add lines 9 and 10'.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation; i4562 p. 5, Line 5: "If line 5 is zero, you cannot elect to expense any section 179 property. In this case, skip lines 6 through 11, enter zero on line 12, and enter the carryover of any disallowed deduction from 2024 (which does not include amounts attributable to qualified section 179 real property) on line 13." The rendered line 10 says "Shown on the values sheet only when: Line 5 is more than zero" (BUG-0155): that is a display condition; the line's value is still the filer's 2024 carryover, and the rendered helper "Add lines 9 and 10" adds it. With line 5 zero, line 9 is zero (the smaller of line 5 and line 8) and line 12 is zero (line 11 is the smaller of income and line 5), so line 13 is the carryover, as the source directs. Checked: classm.s179.2 (line 5 $0, line 10 hidden, $3,000 carryover): project line 13 $3,000.00, which the class M model worked by hand from the pages to the same $3,000.00 (AGREE); the BUG-0155 regression stage14.s179.zero_limit_carryover asserts line 13 $3,000 with line 10 hidden. The model's doubt (whether the hidden line counts as the carryover or as zero) is answered by the English: hiding changes only what is shown, and the English of line 13 says what the page says.
